The planned sweep was part of a new program, what city officials describe as “a revised homeless encampment management plan.”

Under the program, sweeps are happening more frequently than before, on a daily schedule, Monday through Friday. Workers at the city’s Homeless Strategies and Operations Department warn homeless people 72 hours before a sweep is to occur. On the day of the sweep, unhoused people are allowed to take one backpack and one bicycle out of the camp. City workers are directed to confiscate or destroy everything else they own.
In a series of sweeps this past October, homeless people say they lost tents, clothing, medications, identification documents, and other items crucial to their existence.

The public got its first briefing on the new sweeps at a City Council meeting on May 5. The Austin Homeless Strategies and Operations Department said it was creating six teams to clean camps Monday through Friday, each consisting of two APD officers and several employees from Austin Resource Recovery. Three teams would clear out camps in parks, green spaces, and neighborhoods. Two more would clear camps near highways, bridges, and waterways. A sixth would thoroughly clean the areas where camps had been located. HSO emphasized that the city intends to prevent homeless people from returning to camps once they are cleared.
